To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the common fragile sites (FRA3B) are genetically unstable, and that this is caused by the replication of these regions being impaired by DNA polymerase inhibitor aphidicolin.

(i) the replication fork rate is slowed by APH; (ii) FRA3B replication is less efficient and more sensitive to APH than NCFS replication; and (iii) APH treatment results in a greater accumulation of nascent strands at the FRA3 ori 1- 3 than the FRA3B NCFS ori 4.
(i) replication forks are slowed throughout S phase by APH treatment and (ii) the CFS FRA3B is more sensitive to APH-induced slowing of replication than non-fragile sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how cells respond to DNA replication stress.
the replication dynamics of the most frequently induced CFS, FRA 3B.
the mechanisms of DNA replication, the process by which the genetic code is faithfully transmitted from parent to progeny cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CFS replication is impaired in APH-treated cells.
CFSs are more sensitive to APH treatment than NCFSs because the replication forks at the CFSs are less efficient and more sensitive to APHS.
the replication fork is slowed down by the APH, which is a DNA polymerase inhibitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the replication of the FRA3B region is impaired, and that the impairment of replication is more severe when the replication is slowed by aphidicolin.
replication dynamics are impaired at the FRA3b CFS.
the replication fork movement is impaired at the fragile site, which leads to a delay in DNA replication and the formation of the fragile site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the replication dynamics within CFSs are different than those of NCFSs.
the common fragile site FRA3B, which is a large, unstable region of chromosome 3p14.2, contains multiple origins of replication that are active throughout the cell cycle.
the replication fork is not a static entity.
